record.paper_title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
record.original_question: Prove a Paley-Wiener theorem for the Fourier transform of compactly supported H-hyperfunctions, where H denotes the quaternion algebra and H-hyperfunctions are built from boundary values of quaternionic regular functions. The relevant Fourier transform should use the regular quaternionic exponential defined through the homogeneous regular polynomials P_nu, and the theorem should identify compact support with an appropriate space of entire functions of exponential type.

evidence.quote: Problem: Prove a Paley-Wiener Theorem for the Fourier transform of H-hyperfunctions.
The Fourier transform of a H-hyperfunction seems to be a quite complicated object, and the Paley-Wiener theorem ... has not been proved.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the algebra of quaternions, and let $f:\mathbb{H}\to\mathbb{H}$ be (left) regular in the sense of Cauchy–Fueter, i.e. it satisfies
$$\overline{D}f := \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_0} + i\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_1} + j\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_2} + k\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_3} = 0.$$
For each multi-index $\nu$, let $P_\nu(q)$ denote the Fueter homogeneous regular polynomials (the symmetrized products of the Fueter variables $\zeta_\ell = x_\ell - x_0 e_\ell$, $\ell=1,2,3$), and let
$$E(q,\xi) := \sum_{\nu} P_\nu(q)\,\frac{(i\xi)^{|\nu|}}{|\nu|!}\cdot(\text{coefficients})$$
be the regular quaternionic exponential built from the $P_\nu$. The space of $\mathbb{H}$-hyperfunctions on an open set $U\subset\mathbb{R}^4$ is defined as boundary values, modulo regular functions, of Cauchy–Fueter regular functions on appropriate complex neighbourhoods, yielding a sheaf analogous to Sato's hyperfunctions but built from the kernel of $\overline{D}$.

Define the regular Fourier transform $\widehat{T}(\xi)$ of a compactly supported $\mathbb{H}$-hyperfunction $T$ by
$$\widehat{T}(\xi) := \langle T_q, E(q,\xi)\rangle,\qquad \xi\in\mathbb{H}.$$

Problem. Establish a Paley–Wiener theorem characterizing the image of the space of compactly supported $\mathbb{H}$-hyperfunctions under this regular Fourier transform: namely, identify $\widehat{T}$ with an explicitly described space of $\mathbb{H}$-valued entire functions on $\mathbb{H}_{\mathbb{C}}$ of exponential type, with the type bounded by the radius of a ball containing the support of $T$, together with appropriate growth conditions on the real axis reflecting that $T$ is a hyperfunction (rather than a distribution).
artifact.status_search_result: Searches reveal active development of Paley–Wiener-type theorems in quaternionic settings (quaternion Fourier transform, slice regular functions, Dirac operators of Riesz–Feller type), but no source explicitly establishes a Paley–Wiener theorem for compactly supported $\mathbb{H}$-hyperfunctions in the Cauchy–Fueter sense using the regular exponential built from the $P_\nu$. The status of this specific problem could not be confirmed.

status_evidence.title: Paley-Wiener and Boas Theorems for the Quaternion Fourier Transform
status_evidence.snippet: Real Paley-Wiener theorem characterizing quaternion-valued functions whose quaternion Fourier transform has compact support.
status_evidence.claim: A Paley–Wiener theorem exists for the quaternion Fourier transform of functions, but not for $\mathbb{H}$-hyperfunctions via the regular exponential.

status_evidence.title: Paley–Wiener theorems for slice regular functions
status_evidence.snippet: Two Paley–Wiener theorems in the slice regular setting, with reproducing kernel and sampling.
status_evidence.claim: Recent Paley–Wiener results address slice regular (not Cauchy–Fueter hyperfunction) settings.

status_evidence.title: Quaternionic and Clifford Analysis in Several Variables
status_evidence.snippet: Sheaf theoretical approach allowing a rigorous theory of hyperfunctions in the quaternionic domain.
status_evidence.claim: $\mathbb{H}$-hyperfunctions are constructed, but a Paley–Wiener theorem for their Fourier transform is not asserted as proved.
